Hi Alyssa / Ben,

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and agreed next steps so we have alignment on the best deployment mode for FinPay: Hosted API vs Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC.

Summary from our call:
- Primary workload: low-latency transaction classification (~50 QPS peak, 150ms P50 target).
- Current concern: intermittent latency spikes that you suspect are noisy-neighbor related when running heavy batch jobs.
- Security/regulatory: SOC 2 in progress, need audit logs and longer retention for egress logs.

Qualification notes (from our side):
- Hosted API: fastest to go live, shared infra, standard rate limits; suitable if you can tolerate occasional noisy-neighbor variance and leverage our prefix/KV caching.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools with isolation boundaries and prioritized scheduling; recommended if you need stable P50/P95 and capacity guarantees during heavy batch windows.
- Private VPC/on-prem: full network isolation, customer-controlled infra, recommended for strict compliance or when you must control network egress.

Open items / asks for FinPay: please confirm the following so we can recommend a deployment and produce a tailored cost/SLA comparison: 
1) Target SLOs (P50/P95/P99 latency) and acceptable error rates for production.
2) Typical batch windows (times and qps), and whether batch runs are non-negotiable.
3) Data residency or VPC requirements for the audit.
4) Any procurement timeline or prefered start date.

Next steps:
- Marissa will share a short technical note on how Dedicated capacity mitigates noisy-neighbor effects (KV cache isolation, priority scheduling, inference worker pinning).
- I will share a draft SLA and the SOC2 evidence we have available.
- Schedule a follow-up technical call next week (30 min) to deep-dive the P95 behavior and sample traces.

Attaching: Redwood_SLA_Draft_2027-03.pdf (draft SLA), SOC2-Evidence-List.xlsx (items we can provide).

Hi Alyssa, quick technical note as promised. TL;DR: Dedicated capacity gives practical isolation and predictable latency; here are the mechanisms and numbers we've observed.

Key isolation mechanisms in Dedicated capacity:
- Physical/GPU pool reservation: nodes are reserved for your tenancy which removes multi-tenant scheduling contention.
- Inference worker pinning: we pin inference workers to GPU devices and pre-warm KV caches to avoid cold-start jitter.
- Priority scheduling & QoS: production foreground traffic can be placed on higher-priority queues; batch jobs can be limited to run on separate worker sets.
- Networking isolation (for Dedicated in VPC mode): eliminates noisy egress or network saturation from other tenants.

Observed perf (typical for Llama2-style 7B models, mixed-precision quantized):
- 50 QPS, 1k token request: P50 ~120ms, P95 ~220-230ms depending on sequence length and batch alignment.
- Under heavy co-located batch load (shared infra) we've seen P95 spikes >700ms; with Dedicated these spikes are reduced to <300ms in our benchmarks.

Operational notes:
- Autoscaling: Dedicated pools can autoscale with warm-up policies; we recommend pre-scheduled buffer scaling for known batch windows.
- Noisy-neighbor mitigation: if you run large offline batches, we will either schedule them to isolated workers or throttle batch concurrency to maintain foreground SLOs.
- KV cache behavior: prefix caching reduces per-token compute for repeated prompts; Dedicated lets you control cache capacity which helps tail latency for repeated session workloads.

Attachments: technical_playbook_dedicated_vs_shared.md (short doc), I pasted the salient points above; happy to share the full doc if helpful.

If it helps, we can run a 48-hour Dedicated trial (time-limited) against a slice of your traffic to produce an empirical P95 comparison for FinPay.

Thanks Alyssa, answers inline and proposed next steps.

1) P95 guarantees: We don't lock a P95 in the Hosted tier due to multi-tenant variance, but for Dedicated we can commit to an operational target (SLA option) depending on capacity commit. Based on your profile (50 QPS, 1k tokens) the engineering estimate is P95 250-300ms with a 4-node Dedicated pool. I'll run the model and include a 95% confidence band in the SLA draft.

2) Batch windows: Dedicated supports scheduling policies that isolate batch jobs from foreground load. Marissa noted we can either place batch on separate worker sets or throttle concurrency. For FinPay, we recommend:
- Reserve a 20% headroom for foreground traffic during batch windows, and schedule batch jobs on a lower-priority pool.
- If you want stricter isolation, a Dedicated pool with node pinning for production + separate pool for batch is the safest config.

3) Cost delta: ballpark: Dedicated (4-node pool) is ~2.2-2.8x Hosted cost for the same sustained QPS when you factor in reserved capacity and higher SLAs. I'll produce a detailed cost model in the commercial doc.

Procurement/SOC2 evidence: attaching the SOC2 checklist now. If you can confirm the specific controls or documents your procurement team needs, we'll prioritize those.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll send a calendar invite for Tue, Apr 6 at 10:30 PT (30 min) — please confirm or suggest alternatives.
- We'll run an internal cost/SLA calc and deliver the SLA draft + cost model before the call.
- If you'd like, we can provision a 48-hour Dedicated trial the week after the call and capture P95/P99 traces.
